name: hidane official emulator difference database
description: Every place where the official Cloud Firestore emulator, production Firestore and hidane do not all behave the same: what each does, why, the references, and whether hidane reproduces the official emulator or departs from it. Edited by hand; tools/parity/differences.py checks it and writes the tables of docs/parity-exceptions.md.

kinds.meaning: hidane does what the official emulator does, where production Firestore differs.
hidane departs from the official emulator to do what production Firestore or the documented contract does, or to fix what is a bug whatever production does.
hidane departs in a detail clients do not observe or cannot rely on (wording, transport, timing, order, opaque formats), with the same outcome.
hidane departs because it does less, or bounds what the official emulator does not.

differences.official: Batch writes slow down in proportion to the number of stored documents while a listener is attached (reproduced in Phase 0; firebase-tools [#3477](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools/issues/3477)). The cause shows on the Listen stream: after its first answer, every write to a watched collection, even one that changes nothing, is answered with `RESET` and the whole result again
differences.firestore: Listen sends only the documents that entered, changed in or left each target, then one `NO_CHANGE` (the hidane column: "as production does")
differences.hidane: A commit costs O(number of changed documents): Listen sends only the documents that entered, changed in or left each target, then one `NO_CHANGE`, as production does, and nothing for writes that change nothing. 100,000 documents with a whole-collection listener: 4.9 s, flat per batch (`results/listen-batch-writes-hidane.csv`). The SDKs build the same snapshots (`results/sdk-listen-*.json`)
differences.reason: Performance bug, not a semantic contract. See [why.md](why.md) §3

differences.official: A batch that changes a limit query can reach a web SDK listener as two snapshots, the first one showing a document that the same commit deleted
differences.hidane: One snapshot per commit
differences.reason: Bug (snapshots must be atomic)

differences.official: `POST /reset` tells attached listeners nothing, and they receive no later changes either
differences.hidane: Listeners see every document go, then later writes as usual
differences.reason: Bug (listeners keep stale data)

differences.official: A cleared database (`DELETE /emulator/v1/…/documents`, rules-unit-testing's `clearFirestore()`) reaches a web SDK query listener as several snapshots
differences.hidane: One snapshot with every document gone
differences.reason: Follows from answering with `RESET`

differences.official: After a reconnect, the web SDK sees a resumed query in several snapshots: the first still shows the documents deleted or changed away while it was offline, later ones drop them one by one
differences.firestore: Resuming a target sends only what changed since the token (the production table: "Resuming a Listen target")
differences.hidane: One snapshot with everything that changed since the token
differences.reason: Follows from resuming with `RESET` (see the production table below); the SDK then looks up each document it can no longer place. A limit query whose window moved while offline gets one snapshot on both (#146)

differences.official: Adding a Listen target with an ID that is in use ends the stream with `UNKNOWN` and no message
differences.hidane: Ends it with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Target ID … is already in use."
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: A Listen query whose parent names another database reads the stream's database
differences.hidane: Refuses the target (`REMOVE` with an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` cause)
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: Rules conditions are evaluated in two passes, and a denial lists the reasons of both. In the first pass `resource.data` and lookups (`get()`, `exists()`) fail (`evaluation error at L5:22`), the `request.resource` of a write with an update mask or transforms is not computed yet (`debug(request)` shows it as `undefined`, and so does the coverage report's value of `request`, even when the first pass decides), and its lookups count against the limits of 10 and 20 (firebase-tools [#6252](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools/issues/6252), open since 2023). `debug()` prints in both passes, and the coverage report (`:ruleCoverage`) counts both, the first pass's failures as `{"undefined": {}}`
differences.hidane: Evaluate once: a denial lists each statement's reason once, only the conditions' own lookups count, and `debug()` and the coverage report see one evaluation, with `request.resource` always the document as the write leaves it
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: A commit's `verify` write (which the SDKs send for a document a transaction read without writing it) is checked as a `get` in the same two passes, with a different `request` in each: in the first it has the keys of a read (`fields`, null), in the second those of a write (`transforms`, `writeFields`, `readFields`, all null, and `resource`, the stored document). Where the first pass decides, `debug(request)` and the coverage report show the keys of a read
differences.hidane: One evaluation, with the keys of the second pass: `request.resource` is the stored document, and `request.fields` is undefined
differences.reason: Follows from evaluating once, with everything the second pass computes

differences.official: The Emulator UI's request monitor (the WebSocket feed on `--websocket_port`) gets a record for each pass of that evaluation: a first one where `resource` is undefined and conditions reading it fail, then, unless that decided, one with the stored document. An upsert's first pass evaluates `create` and `update`, and if they disagree a third record evaluates the method that applies; `granularAllowOutcomes` grows over all of them
differences.hidane: One record per method evaluated: a read, a document of a batchGet or of a Listen target, a way of a list's filter, a write (an upsert: `create`, then `update`). `resource` holds the stored document (null when there is none)
differences.reason: Follows from evaluating once

differences.official: A client of the request monitor that stops reading holds up every request checked against rules until it reads again or disconnects (recorded: a 256 KiB write did not answer within 5 s)
differences.hidane: Records wait in a queue per client, never the request; a client more than 16 MiB behind is disconnected, and the Emulator UI reconnects and gets the last 50 records
differences.reason: A monitor must not slow down the emulator

differences.official: A request monitor client that connects while its backlog cannot be sent at once (a large backlog) gets it, but no record after it (`BlockingOperationException` in the log)
differences.hidane: Gets the backlog, then every record
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: The WebSocket port does not answer a request for another path than `/requests`, or with a query string
differences.hidane: `404 Not Found`
differences.reason: A request should be answered

differences.official: A Listen query target is checked against the rules again, and recorded, whenever a write changes a document the stream listens to
differences.hidane: Checked once, when it is added (a listened document is checked again when it changes, as on the official emulator)
differences.reason: A query is decided by the query

differences.official: In the coverage report, a `?:` that takes its second branch shows its own value as the value of its first branch (the expressions inside that branch as not evaluated)
differences.hidane: The first branch and everything in it as not evaluated (`{}`)
differences.reason: Bug (a value the branch never had)

differences.official: The coverage report keeps every distinct value of every expression, for as long as the ruleset is loaded; a `request` is a new value each time (it holds the time)
differences.hidane: The first 100 distinct values of each expression are kept and counted; a value that differs from all of them is not counted
differences.reason: Bounded memory: over a long test run the report would otherwise grow without end

differences.official: `GET :ruleCoverage.html` answers a page whose script comes with the official emulator; for an empty project ID, a `500` with an HTML error page
differences.hidane: A page of hidane's own around the same data (`const data = …`, the report's JSON with `<`, `>`, `&`, `=` and `'` escaped as on the official page); for an empty project ID, the `500` of the JSON endpoints
differences.reason: The official page is not redistributable; the data is the same

differences.official: A denied list lists `false` for each way of the filter that was allowed before the denied one (`n == 1` under `n in [1, 2]`: `false for 'list' @ L5, false for 'list' @ L5`)
differences.hidane: The denied way's reasons only
differences.reason: A message reporting allowed ways as `false` misleads

differences.official: A denied commit lists, before the reasons of the write that was denied, the statements of every write checked before it, as `false` even where they allowed it (`c/y` written, then `c/b` verified, under `allow get: if d == 'a'` and `allow create, update: if d == 'y'`: `false for 'create' @ L6, false for 'update' @ L6, false for 'get' @ L5`)
differences.hidane: The denied write's reasons only: the writes are checked in order and the first denied one decides, as on the official emulator
differences.reason: A message reporting allowed writes as `false` misleads

differences.official: Whether a document that a commit writes costs a lookup when another of its writes reads it with `get()` or `exists()` varies from one project to another (commits of the same shape were allowed in some projects and denied in others); through `getAfter()` or `existsAfter()` it never does. A document the commit verifies always costs one through `get()` or `exists()`, and in a verify's condition so does every document the commit writes
differences.hidane: Every document a commit writes is free for its writes' conditions; the rest as on the official emulator
differences.reason: The official result cannot be predicted

differences.official: `replace()` with a replacement Java's regular expressions refuse (`$` alone, a group that does not exist, a trailing `\`) answers `500 UNKNOWN`
differences.hidane: An evaluation error, `Invalid replacement string: <replacement>.`, which denies unless `&&` or `\|\|` absorbs it
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: A string index or slice that cuts a surrogate pair (`'😀'[0]`) gives a string holding half of it
differences.hidane: U+FFFD in its place; sizes and indexes still count UTF-16 code units
differences.reason: A Rust string cannot hold half a pair

differences.official: Transaction conflict detection regressed in v1.22.0 (firebase-tools [#11241](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools/issues/11241))
differences.firestore: Conflicting transactions are detected, as the documented contract says
differences.hidane: Detect conflicts: every document a transaction reads and every collection ID it lists stays locked until it ends; queries will lock the same way (#21)
differences.reason: Bug; parity target is the documented contract

differences.official: A transaction ID is spent on every non-transactional request too, and the count restarts at 1 on `POST /reset`
differences.hidane: Same 9-byte encoding, counted per database, but only transactions take an ID and the count continues across a reset
differences.reason: IDs are opaque to clients. Continuing the count means an ID from before a reset reads as expired instead of naming a new transaction

differences.official: A commit or read with a well-formed transaction ID that was never issued (or was forgotten by a reset) fails with `UNKNOWN` and no message; a rollback answers `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Transaction is invalid or expired."
differences.hidane: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Transaction is invalid or expired." everywhere; an ID that has ended answers `ABORTED` "The referenced transaction has expired or is no longer valid.", as on the official emulator
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: A write that starts waiting for a lock shortly before the holding transaction expires still times out after 2 s: the expiry is only noticed at the next request
differences.hidane: The write proceeds when the holding transaction expires
differences.reason: Timing detail with the same outcome a moment later

differences.official: The Write stream fails with `UNKNOWN` and no message unless the call carries `google-cloud-resource-prefix` or `x-goog-request-params` metadata (every SDK sends one)
differences.hidane: Accepts the stream either way; the database comes from the first request
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: The Write stream handshake accepts any database name
differences.hidane: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a malformed name, as other RPCs answer
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: A write to a document of another database or project is acknowledged, with a write result and a commit time, over gRPC `Commit`, REST `:commit`, `:batchWrite`, a transaction's commit and the Write stream. The document is kept in the request's database under the other name: no read of either database finds it (`GET`, queries), only a batchGet in the request's database that names it, and an export of the request's database holds it, which an import into a database of the other name brings back (`tests/fixtures/commit_checks.json`)
differences.hidane: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Document "…" is not in database "…".", for the whole commit; a batchGet that names a document of another database is refused the same way
differences.reason: Bug (silent data loss)

differences.official: An array union (`appendMissingElements`) whose operand holds an array or a vector with NaN is stored as it is
differences.hidane: Refused when the transform is applied, with the message the value gets in a field ("Nested arrays are not allowed", "Vector cannot contain NaN values.")
differences.reason: Bug (values a document may not hold)

differences.official: An export lists its documents in no particular order
differences.hidane: In name order
differences.reason: The same documents either way ([export-format.md](export-format.md))

differences.official: A seed's documents of another database are kept in the seeded database, where no read finds them, and written into its exports
differences.hidane: Left out
differences.reason: Bug (unreadable data that resurfaces in exports)

differences.official: `find_nearest` reads a vector field path such as `m.v` as one field named `m.v`
differences.firestore: A vector field path such as `m.v` is resolved, the field `v` of the map `m` (the hidane column: "as production and the SDKs do")
differences.hidane: Resolves the path (the field `v` of the map `m`), as production and the SDKs do; `` `m.v` `` names the field `m.v`
differences.reason: Bug (nested vector fields could not be searched)

differences.official: A gRPC message over 100 MiB fails with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` "gRPC message exceeds maximum size 104857600: …"
differences.hidane: Same limit, but tonic answers `OUT_OF_RANGE` "Error, decoded message length too large: …"
differences.reason: Wording of a transport error

differences.official: Server reflection lists `google.firestore.v1beta1.Firestore` (and cannot describe it), `google.firestore.emulator.v1.FirestoreEmulator` and `google.datastore.v1.Datastore`
differences.hidane: Lists `google.firestore.v1.Firestore` and reflection; v1beta1 answers without being listed; the emulator admin API (#36) and Datastore mode (#81) are not served yet
differences.reason: Reflection is for tools; v1beta1 has no descriptors here

differences.official: A document's size is its Datastore entity's encoded size: two string fields pass up to 1,048,486 bytes together
differences.firestore: Firestore's storage size rules: name, field names and values, plus 32 bytes
differences.hidane: Firestore's storage size rules (name, field names and values, plus 32 bytes), which allow a few tens of bytes more
differences.reason: Same limit and message; the exact boundary is an internal encoding

differences.official: WebChannel handshakes and forward-channel answers are chunked and the connection is closed after each
differences.hidane: A content length, and the connection stays open
differences.reason: Transport detail; the client reads the same frames

differences.official: A long-polling back channel puts `noop`s around its first data depending on timing, and ends after one message
differences.hidane: A `noop` while waiting; ends after the messages queued when data comes
differences.reason: Timing; each message arrives once, in order

differences.official: WebChannel sessions are never dropped: each one keeps a thread (firebase-tools [#11124](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools/issues/11124))
differences.hidane: A session with no back channel and no request for 5 minutes is dropped
differences.reason: Bug (resource leak)

differences.official: WebChannel answers carry no `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`
differences.hidane: The CORS headers of every HTTP path, that one included
differences.reason: Harmless

differences.official: JWT segments in `Authorization` are read with a lenient JSON parser (an unquoted key such as `{a:1}` passes)
differences.hidane: Strict JSON: such a token is `invalid jwt`
differences.reason: Clients only send JSON

differences.official: `DELETE /emulator/v1/…/documents/{path}` with an empty path segment names the parent in its error (`Document parent name "…/c/" has invalid trailing "/".`)
differences.hidane: Names the whole path (`Resource name "…" lacks a resource id at index ….`), same status
differences.reason: Wording only

differences.official: RunAggregationQuery responses carry `done: true`, a field the published protos do not define (visible over REST)
differences.hidane: Not sent over gRPC, where clients built from the published protos would drop it; the REST layer (#34) will add it
differences.reason: Not part of the published API

differences.official: REST `GET` of a document or collection with `?transaction=` never answers (gRPC works)
differences.hidane: Follows the gRPC behaviour (#34)
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: A REST query parameter that does not parse (`pageSize=abc`, `showMissing=maybe`) leaves the request unanswered
differences.hidane: `400` "Payload isn't valid for request.", the answer to a body that does not parse
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: A `:listCollectionIds` body that names a `parent` as the path does leaves the request unanswered
differences.hidane: The path wins
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: REST page tokens (`nextPageToken`) are an encoded internal message
differences.hidane: The last name returned, encoded; both are opaque to clients
differences.reason: Internal format

differences.official: ProtoJSON (REST, WebChannel) reads a double through `BigDecimal`: a literal zero such as `-0.0`, `-0` or `"-0"` is `0.0`, but a literal that only rounds to zero, such as `-1e-400`, is `-0.0` (`tools/oracle/negative_zero.py`)
differences.hidane: Every `-0.0` read from ProtoJSON is `0.0`, that one included; gRPC keeps `-0.0` on both
differences.reason: No client writes such a literal, and telling it from `-0.0` would need the number's text, which the JSON parser does not keep

differences.official: iOS clients receive `GOAWAY too_many_pings` after about 90 s (firebase-tools [#11238](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-tools/issues/11238))
differences.firestore: Pinging clients stay connected (the production table: "HTTP/2 keepalive pings")
differences.hidane: Keepalive settings that do not trip the client
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: `PUT :securityRules` without files (`{}`, `{"rules": {"files": []}}`) answers `500` `UNKNOWN` with no message
differences.hidane: `400` "Payload isn't valid for request."
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: A Firestore trigger registration (`…/triggers/{key}`, `…/eventarcTrigger`) with a query parameter that names a field of the trigger (`?eventTrigger.service=…`, `?eventarcTrigger.database=…`) leaves the request unanswered
differences.hidane: The parameter is ignored, as other parameters are
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: A v2 Firestore event's `ce-source` (a function's `event.source`) names the project twice: `//firestore.googleapis.com/projects/projects/{p}/databases/{d}`
differences.firestore: `//firestore.googleapis.com/projects/{p}/databases/{d}` (the hidane column: "as production")
differences.hidane: `//firestore.googleapis.com/projects/{p}/databases/{d}`, as production (`tests/fixtures/function_events.json`, `results/functions-triggers-*.json`)
differences.reason: Bug (a malformed resource name)

differences.official: A write that changes nothing sends v2 `updated` and `written` events whose value and old value are the same, and the delete of a document that does not exist sends v2 `created` and `written` events with neither; v1 triggers get no event for either
differences.firestore: Events only for changes (the why column: "production sends events only for changes")
differences.hidane: No event, for v1 or v2 triggers
differences.reason: Bug: production sends events only for changes, as the official emulator does to v1 triggers

differences.official: `POST /reset` forgets every Firestore trigger the Functions emulator registered: no event reaches it afterwards, and firebase-tools registers triggers only when functions load
differences.hidane: The triggers stay registered, and their events keep reaching the Functions emulator, as after a clear (`DELETE …/documents`), which keeps them on both
differences.reason: Bug (functions stop firing, silently)

differences.official: A v2 trigger registered without a database (firebase-tools always sends one) makes every write to its project answer `500` "Found corrupted Eventarc triggers that have different database", after committing it and sending its v1 events
differences.hidane: The trigger watches `(default)`
differences.reason: Bug (an internal error)

differences.official: The delete events of a deleted path (`DELETE /emulator/v1/…/documents/{path}`) or a cleared database come in no particular order
differences.hidane: In name order
differences.reason: The same events

differences.official: Events go out through Google's HTTP client for Java (`User-Agent: Google-HTTP-Java-Client/…`, `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, kept-alive connections)
differences.hidane: `User-Agent: hidane/<version>`, a connection per event
differences.reason: Transport detail: the Functions emulator reads the path, the content type, the `ce-*` headers and the body

differences.official: Trigger registration bodies are read with a lenient JSON parser: single quotes, unquoted keys, a byte order mark and anything after the first value pass, and a number given for a string keeps its spelling (`1e3`)
differences.hidane: Strict JSON, `400` "Payload isn't valid for request." for the rest; a number as serde_json prints it (`1000.0`)
differences.reason: The Functions emulator sends JSON, with strings (`tests/fixtures/function_triggers.json`)

differences.official: After a syntax error in a ruleset, the error lines that follow the first come from ANTLR's error recovery, which depends on its prediction
differences.hidane: The same first line; the lines after it follow the official recovery where it is simple (every case of `crates/hidane/tests/fixtures/rules_compile.json` matches in full), and can differ elsewhere, such as an unclosed `exists(` around a path literal. Where ANTLR's prediction fails at an earlier token than the lexer's (`{'k':1e+0}` after `==`) or its recovery reads a path (`(…)/-1`), the first line differs too (`crates/hidane-rules/tests/warnings.rs` lists the recorded cases)
differences.reason: Recovery detail; the first error is the one to fix

differences.official: A rule may chain any number of member accesses and indexes (`a.b.c…`, `a[0][0]…`); past about 6,500 the compiler fails with `500` `UNKNOWN`
differences.hidane: More than 2,000 are "Expression is too complex to evaluate safely.", the compiler's message for its other depth limits
differences.reason: Bounds the stack of the parser and the evaluator

differences.official: The `issues[].severity` returned by `:securityRules` is a string (`"ERROR"`) while firebase-tools compares it against a numeric enum, so invalid rules still print "Rules updated."
differences.hidane: hidane returns the same string the official emulator does; the CLI-side comparison is an upstream bug
differences.reason: Keep wire parity; report upstream

differences.official: gRPC reflection lists services but `grpcurl describe` fails on a `google.api.api_visibility` extension
differences.hidane: Full reflection that works with `grpcurl`
differences.reason: Developer convenience

differences.official: `GET //` never answers (the connection hangs)
differences.hidane: `404 Not Found`
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: Precondition failures print the emulator's internal Datastore key: `entity already exists: EntityRef[partitionRef=dev~p, path=/c/d]`, and a protobuf text dump of the key for `no entity to update`
differences.firestore: `Document already exists: <name>` and `No document to update: <name>`
differences.hidane: Production Firestore's wording, `Document already exists: <name>` and `No document to update: <name>`; same status codes (`ALREADY_EXISTS`, `NOT_FOUND`)
differences.reason: Internal detail; applications see the production wording in production

differences.official: `read_time` older than at least two hours is still served (the exact limit is #86)
differences.firestore: `read_time` up to one hour old (the hidane column: "like production Firestore")
differences.hidane: Up to one hour old, like production Firestore; older answers `FAILED_PRECONDITION` "The requested 'read_time' is too old." with the official message
differences.reason: Bounded memory for old versions (ADR 0002)

differences.official: The REST `readTime` parameter always fails with "Only timestamps past epoch are supported.", even for the latest commit time (gRPC works)
differences.hidane: Follows the gRPC behaviour (#34)
differences.reason: Bug

differences.official: With `--single_project_mode` (which firebase-tools passes unless `emulators.singleProjectMode` is `false`), a request for a project ID other than `--project_id` is served and a warning is logged, as the flag's `--help` text says (`crates/hidane/src/cli.rs`); with `--single_project_mode_error`, its help says the mismatch is an error instead. The warning's wording is not recorded
differences.hidane: Accepts both flags and requires `--project_id` with `--single_project_mode`, as the official emulator does, then serves every project ID without a warning or an error
differences.reason: Not implemented: firebase-tools does not pass `--single_project_mode_error` (it is not among the Firestore emulator's arguments in its `src/emulator/downloadableEmulators.ts`), so under it the difference is a log line, and requests are answered the same. `hidane doctor` reports it for projects in single project mode

differences.official: `serverTimestamp()` stores the time the request was received, truncated to milliseconds, a few milliseconds before the commit time
differences.hidane: The commit time truncated to milliseconds
differences.reason: Same precision and the same value for every field of a commit; tests cannot depend on which instant inside the request is used

differences.official: A JSON string holding an unpaired surrogate (`\ud800`) is stored, as a value, a map key, a field path or a document name; reads print it as `?`
differences.hidane: `400` "Payload isn't valid for request.", the answer to a body that does not parse
differences.reason: hidane's strings are UTF-8, as protobuf strings over gRPC must be, and UTF-8 cannot hold an unpaired surrogate; no SDK writes one (#262)

differences.official: Timestamps are read leniently, in values, preconditions and read times: a field out of range rolls over into the next (`2020-13-01T00:00:00Z` is 2021-01-01, hour `24` the next day, second `60` the next minute, an offset of `+24:00` a day), and fields of other widths are read (`2020-1-01`, `20-01-01`, `00.Z`)
differences.hidane: RFC 3339, strictly: four digits for the year and two for each other field, each in range; anything else is `400` "Payload isn't valid for request." A leap second (`:60`), which RFC 3339 allows, is read as `:59`
differences.reason: The API documents timestamps as RFC 3339, which has no month 13; a lenient read turns a client's mistake into another time (#262)

differences.official: A RunQuery or RunAggregationQuery that begins a read-write transaction (`newTransaction`) and fails a check made once the transaction has begun (a negative limit or offset, a field ordered twice, …) answers the error and leaves the transaction open, its ID never sent: its lock on the queried collection makes the next write there wait 2 s and fail with `ABORTED` "Transaction lock timeout.", until the transaction expires
differences.hidane: A request that fails begins no transaction and locks nothing
differences.reason: Bug (a lock no client can release) (#262)

differences.official: A `POST` whose `Content-Type` is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data` gets a bare `404 Not Found` (plain text, no content type) on every REST path (`:commit`, `:runQuery`, a create, …), whatever its body; `PATCH`, `GET` and `DELETE` with those types are served
differences.hidane: Serves it, reading the body as JSON as for any other content type
differences.reason: A `404` for a path that exists misleads; no SDK sends a form to these paths (#262)

differences.official: A request whose request line (method, path with its query string, `HTTP/1.1`) is longer than 4,096 bytes gets a bare `404 Not Found`, whatever the path: a `GET` of a document is served up to a path of 4,084 bytes. A document ID of 751 `é`, percent-encoded, is already longer
differences.hidane: Serves paths of up to 65,534 bytes, as any other request (a longer one gets `414 URI Too Long`); an ID over 1,500 bytes in one is refused with the official message, "The key path element name is longer than 1500 bytes."
differences.reason: A `404` for a path that exists misleads; the limit is on the request line, not on what the API accepts (#262)

differences.official: Locks, measured in #17: a read-write transaction holds a shared lock on every document it reads (found or not) and on every collection with a collection ID it lists or queries, whatever the parent. A write, in a transaction or not, waits for other transactions' locks for up to 2 s, then fails with `ABORTED` "Transaction lock timeout." (which ends a waiting transaction). An unused transaction expires 60 s after its last request (the [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/emulator) say 30 s). `concurrency_mode: OPTIMISTIC` is accepted and ignored. Read-only transactions lock nothing and read the snapshot of their start
differences.firestore: Contention is resolved by aborting a transaction with `ABORTED` rather than by a fixed wait, and optimistic concurrency can be selected
differences.hidane: As the official emulator: the same lock scope, waits, expiry and messages
differences.reason: Follow the official emulator: same lock scope, waits, expiry and messages (`tests/fixtures/transactions.json`, replayed by `crates/hidane/tests/transactions.rs`)
